references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the LORD's dwelling and his altar are mentioned, showing the connection to the fear of building a competing altar.
Moses warned against offering burnt offerings on any place, but only at the place the LORD chooses – a fundamental law underlying the concern in this text.
The law forbids offering sacrifices at places other than the entrance of the tabernacle, which explains why the tribes defend themselves against accusations of rebellion.
Warning against turning away from the LORD – the same expression about 'turning away' from following the LORD is used here.
The people declare that it is unthinkable ('far be it from us') to abandon the LORD – the same strong rejection of apostasy.
Samuel uses a similar expression: 'Far be it from me to sin against the LORD' – the same Hebrew expression 'chalilah'.
The altar for burnt offerings was placed in front of the tabernacle, which is mentioned here as 'the altar that stands before his dwelling'.
